scope: 50,000 LEDs: production sender characterization; real OpenRGB/preview fixes; isolated E1.31 and temporal scheduling prototypes; paced and maximum-throughput full effect catalogs.

method.sender_trials: Three repetitions, 2 seconds for stock/fixed, 3 seconds for prototype. Dense deterministic float64 input. Encoding and loopback separate. Target 60 FPS paced runs separate from saturation.
method.loopback: 127.0.0.2 verified real local loopback; receiver CPU excluded from sender CPU.
method.effect_trials: One 2-second measurement after 1-second warmup per effect, synthetic PCM, media/screen fixtures, full websocket pixels, standard asyncio, fake DDP device. Screening results, not repeated causal comparisons. Effective refresh rate rounded by LedFx.
limitations: Single WSL2 host; no physical LED, firmware, LAN or Wi-Fi claims.
Sender timing excludes rendering and websocket work. CPU percentages use 100% for one core.
Per-pixel OSC at 50k produces 50k or 150k datagrams per frame; 2-second windows contain few frames, so inspect ranges.
Prototype changes only benchmark-local sACN output/packet instances. It is not enabled by LedFx or a released dependency.
Adalight is encoding only: at default 500000 baud/8N1, 150006 bytes imply a theoretical ceiling around 0.333 FPS.
Initial unpaced pilot used a receiver thread and unusual 127.0.0.1 route; it lost complete DDP frames and is retained as a diagnostic only.
max-catalog is an interrupted diagnostic with all fixture threads also unpaced. max-target is the completed corrected catalog. Do not rank Blender/Radial using the aborted diagnostic.
Temporal on-demand prototype changes animation timing: it ignores effect_loop timing multipliers/speed pacing. It is not production code.

Synthetic audio updates at 60 Hz, so some effects generate only about 60 distinct images/s even when transport FPS is much higher. Static outputs similarly do not become useful new images simply by retransmission.
method.maximum_fps: Target render/temporal sleeps replaced by scheduler yields; fixture threads retain pacing. Preview cap bypassed only in benchmark workers (1M FPS). Configured effective_refresh_rate is not a ceiling in these rows. Independent DDP receiver process, IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.2. Report changed websocket frames separately from repeated frames.
method.confirmation: Three 3-second repetitions of Fade, Rainbow, Smoke 2D and Melt & Sparkle with/without full streaming. Temporal on-demand prototype: Fade/Rainbow full streaming, three 3-second repetitions. CPU sampling uses separate five-second runs.
method.preview_comparison: Same new harness/receiver/loopback, three four-second repeats at normal pacing, baseline repository f075f3af versus phase-scheduled preview. No schema/rate-cap change.

findings: 50k OpenRGB exposed ignored partial TCP writes. Three initial loopback runs failed stream validation. A diagnostic reproduced two short writes and ten invalid packets. Production now uses socket.sendall; corrected runs retain identical packet bytes.

Experimental sACN adapter converts the built-in int list produced by E131Device to bytes with C-level range validation, then uses an immutable-byte packet setter with tuple padding. Public transport/sync machinery remains unchanged; out-of-range channels are rejected.

Preview rate limiting reset its timer to each accepted frame, causing a 62 FPS source to fall near half the requested 60 FPS preview rate. Monotonic scheduled deadlines fix this while skipping missed slots and preventing duplicate-time/catch-up bursts. Four deterministic rate tests failed before the fix.

At maximum throughput the old receiver thread competed with websocket decoding and lost UDP frames. The benchmark now isolates DDP collection in a separate process and rejects baseline comparisons across different receiver/pacing/bind scenarios.

Unpacing a fixture virtual overwhelmed Blender: the aborted diagnostic delivered ~39 FPS; correctly scoping unpaced work to the target measured ~373 FPS. This is a benchmark correction, not a claimed application speedup.
Matched normal-pacing preview medians: Rainbow 32.74 -> 60.20 FPS; Melt and Sparkle 34.24 -> 59.98; Noise 2D 32.99 -> 60.20. Retained render cadence and packet bytes.

validation.scope: Accumulated performance suite, prototype packet equivalence and instance isolation, full 50k TCP partial-write regression, frozen schemas, static checks.
validation.static_checks: Ruff, ClassVar audit and strict Pyrefly baseline ratchet pass; no suppressions added.

reproduce: Use --senders e131 --e131-bytes-prototype --seconds 3 for isolated byte-buffer comparison. Add --modes encode --sampling cpu --seconds 4 --repeats 1 to profile stock and prototype separately.
For repeated limits use --effects fade,rainbow,smoke2d,melt_and_sparkle --streams none,full --seconds 3 --repeats 3.

For the temporal experiment use --effects fade,rainbow --streams full --temporal-render with both unpaced flags. Add --sampling cpu --seconds 5 --repeats 1 for separate profiles, then tools/effect_profile_report.py.

next_priorities.evidence: 132-trial extension: around 2.4–2.5x encoding and 1.6x loopback E1.31 throughput across dense/sparse/static input, with expanded layout/dtype equivalence checks.
next_priorities.proposal: Seek an upstream supported immutable-byte setter; leave the private experiment confined to tools.

next_priorities.evidence: 59.38% of active CPU samples in Smoke2d.draw at 50k.
next_priorities.proposal: Separate coordinate construction from native noise generation, then investigate batched/native optimizations without reducing noise octaves or visual quality.

next_priorities.evidence: 23.28% triangle, 17.20% array_sin; repeated full-stream delivery ~166.89 FPS.
next_priorities.proposal: Profile/reuse numeric workspaces or fuse kernels with exact numeric-reference tests before claiming gains.

next_priorities.evidence: 51.49% of active samples in DDPDevice.send_packet after the Fade on-demand prototype.
next_priorities.proposal: Measure packet construction separately from socket calls; batching needs portable transport/receiver compatibility work.

extended_experiments.conclusion: Cadence-controlled results do not justify a production temporal scheduler rewrite; sACN bytes path retains a repeatable gain. See experiments.json for paired ranges, animated cases, semantic validation and limits.

earlier_next_priorities.evidence: Repeated full-stream Fade delivery 91.14 -> 575.57 FPS, changed images 90.81 -> 503.91; Rainbow delivery 333.81 -> 443.55 FPS with server CPU ~160% -> ~107%.
earlier_next_priorities.proposal: Elapsed-time-driven temporal effects computed on demand, or a bounded producer/consumer handoff. Preserve speed/multiplier semantics, shutdown and transition behavior before promoting prototype.
